problem: Graph-based VLN methods (DUET, BEVBert, PRET) encode visual appearance and angular cues in one entangled feature space, and treat the instruction as a holistic input, so they do not explicitly extract navigation-critical location and object semantics. This leads to imprecise spatial reasoning and weak cross-modal alignment.
motivation: Directional reasoning and visual perception play different roles in navigation, so mixing them causes interference. Instructions contain decision-relevant location descriptors (room types) and object references (landmarks) that generic cross-attention over the whole instruction may dilute, especially for long, instruction-dense trajectories.
key_idea: Decouple angular and visual cues and add geometric embeddings on directed graph edges (observation-graph interaction), and explicitly extract LLM-derived location and object vocabularies from the instruction to guide cross-modal fusion (key-detail guidance).
insight: The ablation on R2R val-unseen shows gains that build up step by step: MED gives SR 73.32 to 74.13, GE gives 74.70, location details give 74.78, and object details give 75.54 (SPL 63.07 to 65.60, NE 3.01 to 2.68). Inference time only rises from 3.69 to 4.08 ms. The theoretical analysis (gradient-variance and mutual-information bounds) is asserted with proofs only in supplementary material, so it gives no independent evidence.
method: Observation-Graph Interaction (decoupling): angular and visual components of the panoramic observation features are embedded separately (E_a, E_v), concatenated and fused by an MLP to give F'_o.

Geometric positional embedding: for each candidate, the heading difference to the observation views (atan2 of sin/cos difference) gives the closest angular distance d'. A linear projection of [d', sin, cos] gives pe, which is added to a linear embedding of [sin/cos heading, sin/cos elevation] to form the directed-edge features F'_g.

Edge update: a transformer decoder layer with candidate/edge features as queries and F'_o as keys/values updates the directed graph G'_t. Visual features come from DINOv2, and the graph is a directed one built incrementally, as in PRET.

Key-Detail Guidance: an LLM preprocesses the instruction corpus into location and object vocabularies. The matching token features from a pretrained-LM text encoder are projected by E_L and E_O and fused into F_k.

Cross-modal enhancement: the graph and the instruction are fused by a multi-layer transformer decoder to give F_c. F_c then cross-attends to F_k (queries F_c, keys/values F_k) with a linear projection, followed by a residual connection, self-attention over candidates, and an MLP that scores candidates. The highest-scoring candidate is chosen as the next node.

Training: MLM pretraining (15% masking, 100k iterations), then fine-tuning for 200k iterations with a mix of teacher forcing and student forcing (lambda=0.2). Recovery pseudo-labels use the nearest unvisited GT node or the shortest path. Augmented R2R/RxR data from prior work is used.

setting.backbone: DINOv2 visual encoder + pretrained-LM text encoder + transformer decoders (trained; OIKG on a PRET-style directed graph)
setting.training_data: R2R and RxR training data plus augmented data from prior works; MLM pretraining then fine-tuning
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discretized views per viewpoint) with heading/elevation angles
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (candidate node selection over a directed graph)
setting.privileged: none (an LLM is used offline to build location/object vocabularies from the instruction corpus)

results: OIKG reaches R2R val-unseen SR 75 / SPL 65 / NE 2.68 and test-unseen SR 74 / SPL 64 / NE 3.05, roughly matching or slightly beating PRET (74/65, 72/64) and BEVBert/GridMM (75/64). On RxR val-unseen it gets SR 74.7 / nDTW 74.8 / sDTW 64.2, beating PRET (72.8/73.4/62.4).
limitations: Relies on location and object vocabularies built offline with an LLM, which may not generalize to novel terminology.
Evaluated only in simulation on discrete-graph R2R/RxR; no continuous-environment or real-robot tests.
R2R gains over PRET are marginal, and the theorems have only asserted proofs in the supplementary material.
